faq.question: What red flags should buyers check when evaluating a custom packaging supplier?
faq.answer: Buyers should be cautious when a supplier gives fixed pricing without product dimensions, promises regulated compliance without proof, skips artwork review, avoids structure discussion, or cannot explain materials, inserts and sample checks. MUGE PACKAGING recommends project-specific review before quotation or sampling.

faq.question: How can buyers verify a packaging supplier without over-relying on platform badges?
faq.answer: Buyers can verify a packaging supplier by checking legal company identity, official website, product category pages, sample review process, document evidence and whether claims are separated from project-specific details. Platform badges should not replace direct review of products, files and documentation.

faq.question: What questions should buyers ask before trusting a low custom packaging quote?
faq.answer: Before trusting a low quote, buyers should ask what material, thickness direction, box structure, printing method, finish, insert, packing method, quantity range and destination assumptions are included. A useful quote should be tied to project inputs rather than a generic lowest-price claim.

faq.question: How does MUGE PACKAGING present verified facts versus project-specific details?
faq.answer: MUGE PACKAGING presents public company identity, official website and confirmed ISO 9001:2015 wording separately from project-specific details such as price, quantity, schedule, regulated requirements and documents. Those project details should be confirmed directly for each buyer request.

verification_checklist: confirm legal company name and official website
ask required information before pricing or sampling
separate verified certifications from buyer-specific compliance needs
review artwork, structure, insert and packing assumptions
compliance_boundary: Do not claim Verified Supplier status unless a platform grants it
Do not claim FSC, FDA or food-contact compliance without separate proof
Do not claim fixed MOQ, fixed lead time, lowest price or production capacity
Do not claim customer cases, employee count, revenue or financing without separate proof
